text.p: Electropharmacology Inc said on Friday that its purchase-distribution agreement with National Patient Care Systems Inc has been terminated effective as of July 18, 1997 after a change in Medicare reimbursement policy.

The U.S. Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) established a new policy to deny Medicare reimbursement for the use of all electrical stimulation, including pulsed electromagnetic fields, in treating wounds.
Electropharmacology, maker of SofPulse a treatment for pain and edema, and National Patient may jointly explore selected market opportunities for SofPulse in the U.S. under a separate agreement.
Electropharmacology said in a statement that it reacquired the marketing rights and control of its fleet of SofPulse devices from National Patient.

Electropharmacology will continue to focus on international markets and pursue alternative marketing strategies, including lease-purchase or sale of SofPulse devices to customers in the United States.
The Health Care Financing Administration's policy applies to the use of electrical stimulation in the promotion of wound healing, the company said.
